objective: T-20260929-70: does net share issuance NSI252 = ln(shares_t / shares_{t-252}) (low issuance is long) predict the cross-section of returns in the ADV top-1500 pool (price >= 5) after next-open entry, in the 2024+ window and the full 2017-2026 sample, and is it distinct from size and 12-1 momentum? Only if the cheap IC test passes are 8 preregistered long-only / long-short books screened at 10/20 bp with borrow.

sources.core_claim: QuanterLab 2026-08-19 (author-run, S&P 500 point-in-time, 20 sealed windows 2006-2025, net of costs): the low-net-issuance book earns 10.58%/yr, Sharpe 0.58, versus the reference index 9.51%/yr, Sharpe 0.54, and beats the earnings-yield book in only 35 of 100 bootstrap paths, which the author calls a statistical tie.
sources.project_applicability: Only recent published test of a net-issuance long book: a tie with the index, so the plain long-only large-cap version adds nothing; the local question is the cross-section in a broad top-1500 pool since 2024 and the short leg.
sources.reflection: Full page text saved as snapshot; table row quoted verbatim in the source card. Limitations: Author-run platform study of a 30-name low-share-growth long-only S&P 500 book with annual reselection; no borrow or short leg, no 2024+ split, cover-page share counts are not used (weighted shares from filings); second source QuantDecoded (Pontiff-Woodgate 2008 summary) was blocked by a Vercel checkpoint on 2026-09-29 (HTTP 429), so it is claim_only and no number from it is used.

sources.core_claim: Pontiff and Woodgate (JF 2008): post-1970, share issuance has a strong cross-sectional ability to predict stock returns, more significant than size, book-to-market or momentum individually; pre-1970 no significant ability for most holding periods.
sources.project_applicability: Origin of the sign and the horizon logic (issuance -> lower returns); sample ends 2003 so it says nothing about 2024+.
sources.reflection: Abstract page opened; effect sizes (decile returns) not read in primary text, so no target is taken from it.

sources.core_claim: Fama and French (JF 2008) Dissecting Anomalies: anomalous returns associated with net stock issues, accruals and momentum are pervasive across micro, small and big size groups; for net stock issues, extreme positive issues are followed by negative abnormal returns but less extreme positive issues are typically followed by positive abnormal returns.
sources.project_applicability: Supports testing a broad pool, size-group tiers and a residualization on size; the non-monotonic middle deciles warn that a quintile long/short may be noisier than the extremes.
sources.reflection: Tool returned a truncated abstract; the chinks-in-the-armor sentence comes from a search result snippet (claim_only).

sources.core_claim: Hou, Xue and Zhang (RFS 2020): with microcaps alleviated via NYSE breakpoints and value-weighted returns, 286 of 447 anomalies (64%) are insignificant at 5%; capital markets are more efficient than previously recognized.
sources.project_applicability: Warns that an equal-weight top-1500 cross-section can be a microcap-tilted effect: the local IC gate reports by-tier IC and the residual on size.
sources.reflection: Abstract quoted; net stock issues specific result not read.

sources.core_claim: Daniel and Titman: intangible information reliably predicts future returns, tangible returns have no forecasting power; premia associated with intangible information challenge traditional and psychological models.
sources.project_applicability: Background for the composite-issuance idea (equity issuance as an intangible-return proxy); JF 2006 abstract in the search result mentions a composite issuance measure independently forecasting returns (claim_only).
sources.reflection: NBER abstract opened; composite-issuance sentence only from a search snippet.

sources.core_claim: Loughran and Ritter (JF 1995): 1970-1990 IPO and SEO issuers earned only 5% and 7% per year over five years after issue; book-to-market explains only a modest part of the low returns.
sources.project_applicability: Mechanism for the issuer (short) leg: event-level issuance; NSI252 is a diluted, all-issuance proxy for it.
sources.reflection: Abstract quoted; event study, not a tradable cost-adjusted result.

sources.core_claim: Ikenberry, Lakonishok and Vermaelen (1995): 1980-1990 open-market repurchase announcements were followed by 12.1% average abnormal four-year buy-and-hold return, 45.3% for value stocks.
sources.project_applicability: Buyback side of the same mechanism; announcement-level, not the share-count change tested here.
sources.reflection: Seen only in a search summary, claim_only; no number is used as a target.

sources.core_claim: McLean and Pontiff (JF 2016): across 97 predictors, portfolio returns are 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower post-publication.
sources.project_applicability: Prior that a 2008-published anomaly has decayed by 2024 and that decay is concentrated where trading is easy; the 2024+ window is the honest test.
sources.reflection: Seen only in a search summary, claim_only.

candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: A long-only low-issuance large-cap book is a published tie with the index, so books are built only if a cross-sectional IC survives on 2024+; the short/hedged variants test whether the edge sits in the issuer leg.
